messages:
linh-support: FYI customer ACME reported ~2k audit events missing from their Splunk sink for 2026-02-10 22:00-23:30 UTC. They attached a sample zip we pulled from their S3 export.

linh-support: key details — manifest exists, but several .gz files are 0 bytes and a few have header mismatch errors when we try to gunzip. Customer says they did a full replay attempt and Splunk only ingested ~60% of expected events.

sam-eng-security: can you attach the sample zip link? also any KMS rekey activity around that window?

linh-support: link: s3://redwood-exports/acme/2026-02-10/zone-3/sample-repro.zip (internal). No KMS rotation recorded in our DB for that tenant at the timestamp, but the customer says they rotated their tenant alias in their KMS at ~22:05 UTC.

arjun-eng-sre: quick check: zero-byte blobs usually mean the manifest referenced object was uploaded but the multipart put failed or the uploader wrote a 0-byte placeholder. But header mismatch + gunzip errors => content truncated or wrong content-encoding.

tess-support: attaching the unzip log I ran: 
```
$ unzip -l sample-repro.zip
inflating: events-20260210-2205.gz  0 bytes
inflating: events-20260210-2210.gz  12,384 bytes
$ gunzip events-20260210-2210.gz
gzip: events-20260210-2210.gz: invalid header
```

maya-ps: audit-bot shows this export job had two retries and a deferred flush at 22:07 due to transient 5xx from the storage layer. job_id=exp-9f3b, attempt=3. I can paste the job trace.

audit-bot: export-job exp-9f3b status=partial_success retries=3 deferred_flush=true storage_err_count=2 kms_err_count=0 manifest_entries=1200 gz_files=1200 zero_byte_files=7

sam-eng-security: ok, candidate hypothesis: uploader attempted to write encrypted payload using a KMS envelope with the customer's alias. If the tenant rotated their alias mid-upload and the client SDK retried with a new cipher envelope, some parts may be encrypted with the new key while manifest references or metadata still point to old envelope headers, causing consumers to fail decryption or treat bytes as invalid -> gzip header errors.

arjun-eng-sre: steps to repro locally: 1) simulate a two-part upload where part1 encrypted with keyA, part2 with keyB; 2) assemble into single .gz and try gunzip -> should error. Recommend trying `aws s3 cp` the object and run `file -b` to inspect content header.

linh-support: I ran `file events-20260210-2210.gz` — result: "data" (not "gzip compressed data"). so header was wiped or corrupted. Also noticed object metadata `x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id` present for some parts and missing for others.

tess-support: customer asked for actionable next steps for Splunk replay. Proposed playbook: 1) run object-level validation and rebuild gz files from raw JSON parts where possible; 2) for zero-byte objects, check S3 object versions and try to fetch prior version; 3) if KMS alias rotation caused mixed envelopes, coordinate with customer to temporarily re-add old alias (or provide rewrap keys) to decrypt and replay.

sam-eng-security: agree. add: provide a signed presigned-get for sample bad objects and our SRE team will attempt rewrap/decrypt in a safe offline environment. Also request KMS CloudTrail logs from the customer for +-10m around 22:00 to confirm alias rotate timing.

maya-ps: I'll kick off a limited replay plan with customer: (a) we will attempt to fetch prior object versions (b) attempt best-effort recompose of missing gz by concatenating valid parts (c) if we can recover >95% events, schedule targeted replay to Splunk. If not recoverable, propose backfill from primary event store via our export backfill job.

linh-support: customer asked about billing for replay — pls confirm if backfill uses on-demand export credits or will be treated as support-assisted restore (possible charge).

arjun-eng-sre: operational note: when our export job defers flush due to storage 5xx we buffer to temporary local store and then flush later. There is an edge where buffer finalization writes an empty object on crash. I'll open an infra issue to add extra integrity checks (crc on manifest vs object) to avoid zero-byte placeholders.

sam-eng-security: create follow-up ticket for infra (ENG-INFRA-xxxx) and link to this thread. Also escalate to compliance: if events are missing for that tenant, we must log retention windows and communicate SLA impact.

tess-support: customer is asking for a concise repro summary to hand to their security team. Drafting reply: "We observed mixed/envelope inconsistencies and transient storage failures during export. Our SRE will attempt version recovery and rewrap operations. If full recovery isn't possible, we will run a targeted backfill and share a post-mortem. Awaiting your KMS CloudTrail logs and confirmation to attempt rewrap." Thoughts?

sam-eng-security: wording looks good. add that we will not store decrypted customer data beyond troubleshooting window and will perform operations in customer-provided VPC if they require.

linh-support: I'll send that to the customer and request KMS logs + permission to attempt decryption/replay. Marking thread P1 until we confirm recovery or backfill schedule. :warning:
